::: {.lead}
Today the lab computers are Rami's desk. Each student gets the same build,
`PocketQuest_1.3.apk`, and the same test plan with eight test cases; one of
them hides a real bug. There are no new ideas: you use what Lecture 13
taught to create an Android Virtual Device, start it, install the build,
run a test case, collect the evidence and write a bug report. Work on a lab
computer or in Emulator Lab. The results of the activities are at the end
of this worksheet: try first, then compare.
:::

## Recall

- An **AVD** is a device profile (screen, RAM) plus a **system image** (one
  Android version, for example API 30); it runs in the Android Emulator.
- **adb** talks to the emulator or the phone: `adb devices`, `adb install`,
  `adb logcat`.
- An emulator is good for versions and sizes, not for speed, heat or
  sensors.
- A test result names the build, the device and the OS version.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="a USB cable|the Play Store"}
What gives an AVD its Android version?
:   the system image

    Why: One system image is one Android version.

Which command lists the connected devices and emulators?
:   adb devices

    Why: adb talks to every connected device.

What can an emulator not test well?
:   the heat of a long race

    Why: It runs on the computer, not on a phone.
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · Create and start the virtual device

Each student gets the same build, `PocketQuest_1.3.apk`, and the same test
plan with eight test cases. Steps 1–3 happen in Android Studio:

1. **Device Manager** › **Create device**.
2. Choose the device profile and the **system image** (downloaded once);
   name the AVD, for example `P5_API_30`.
3. Press **Start**. The first start (a **cold boot**) takes longer; later
   starts use a saved state (**quick boot**). From a terminal:
   `emulator -list-avds` lists the AVDs, `emulator -avd P5_API_30` starts
   one.

![The steps of the seminar.](images/seminar-steps.png){width=90%}

{{< sim file="sims/adb-lab.html" poster="sims/adb-lab.png" title="Emulator Lab: run Pocket Quest 1.3" height="720" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
If the emulator does not start, virtualization may be off in the BIOS, or
the computer has too little free RAM. Close other programs, and ask the lab
technician.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Start P5_API_30 · 10 min"}
On the lab computer (or in **Emulator Lab**, Task 1), create and start
`P5_API_30`: 720 × 1600, 4 GB, Android 11. Write how long the first boot
took.

*Your product:* a running emulator and one time.

::: {.check}
The emulator shows the home screen of Android 11. A first (cold) boot takes
about 15–60 seconds on a lab PC; the next starts are faster (quick boot).
In Emulator Lab, Task 1 is done when `emulator -list-avds` shows
`P5_API_30` and the AVD has started.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Steps 1–3"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the Play Store|a USB cable"}
Where do you create an AVD in Android Studio?
:   the Device Manager

    Why: The Device Manager creates, starts and deletes AVDs.

What is the slow first start of an AVD called?
:   a cold boot

    Why: Later starts use a saved state: a quick boot.

Which command lists the AVDs?
:   emulator -list-avds

    Why: It prints the names of all AVDs.
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · Install the build

Step 4 puts the build on the emulator. Two ways:

- **Drag and drop** the `.apk` file onto the emulator window.
- **adb:** `adb devices` must list the emulator (for example
  `emulator-5554 device`); then `adb install PocketQuest_1.3.apk`. `adb
  uninstall` with the package name removes the app.
- `adb: no devices/emulators found` means the emulator is not running.
  `failed to stat … No such file` means adb is in the wrong folder.

![Commands of the seminar.](images/adb-commands.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Two installs · 8 min"}
Install the build twice: once by drag and drop, once with `adb install`
(uninstall it in between). In Emulator Lab, do Tasks 2 and 3. Copy the
output of `adb devices`.

*Your product:* two installs and one line of output.

::: {.check}
`adb devices` shows `List of devices attached` and `emulator-5554
device`. `adb install PocketQuest_1.3.apk` prints `Success`, and the Pocket
Quest icon appears. If you see `no devices/emulators found`, start the
emulator first.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Installing"}
Use Emulator Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Restart the router|Buy a phone"}
adb: no devices/emulators found. What do you do?
:   start the emulator first

    Why: adb can install only on a running device.

What does adb print after a good install?
:   Success

    Why: Then the game's icon appears on the emulator.

failed to stat … No such file. What is wrong?
:   adb is in the wrong folder

    Why: Run adb in the folder of the APK, or write the full path.
:::
:::

## Activity 3 · Run the test case and collect evidence

Steps 5 and 6: test, and keep the proof.

- Follow the test plan **in order**, and mark each case pass or fail.
- The emulator's **extended controls** change the device: rotation, the
  battery, the location, the network speed and delay, a phone call.
- Keep the **evidence**: a **screenshot** of the problem and the lines of
  **Logcat** (`adb logcat`) around the moment it happened.
- Repeat a failed case once, to be sure that the steps make it happen
  again.

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Do not copy the whole log: copy the lines around the error, with the time.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 3 · Test case 7 · 12 min"}
Test case 7: "Start a race, then turn the device to landscape."

1. Run it in Emulator Lab (Tasks 4 and 5) or on your AVD.
2. Read the log, take a screenshot, and repeat the case once.

*Your product:* a screenshot, the error line, and pass or fail.

::: {.check}
The race freezes when the device turns to landscape; after a few seconds
Android says *Pocket Quest isn't responding*. The log shows `E/Unity:
NullReferenceException: RaceHud.OnScreenRotate () (at RaceHud.cs:118)`.
The case **fails**, and it fails again when repeated.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Test case 7"}
Use Emulator Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the battery|the font"}
What freezes the race?
:   turning to landscape

    Why: The error comes from OnScreenRotate.

Which file does the error name, and at which line?
:   RaceHud.cs, line 118

    Why: The log line shows the file and the line.

Why do you repeat a failed case?
:   to be sure it happens again

    Why: A bug that the steps repeat can be fixed.
:::
:::

## Activity 4 · Write the bug report

Step 7: a developer must be able to repeat the bug from the report alone.

- **Title:** what goes wrong, in one line.
- **Build:** the version and the build number. **Device:** the AVD or phone
  and its OS version.
- **Steps:** numbered, from the start. **Expected** and **actual** result.
- **Attached:** the screenshot and the lines of the log. One bug per
  report.
- Facts, not opinions: "the race freezes", not "the HUD code is bad".

![A good bug report.](images/bug-report.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 4 · Your bug report · 10 min"}
Write the bug report of test case 7 with all its parts.

*Your product:* one complete bug report.

::: {.check}
A good report: **Title:** The race freezes when the device turns to
landscape. **Build:** PocketQuest_1.3, build 42. **Device:** AVD
P5_API_30, Android 11. **Steps:** 1. Start a race. 2. Turn the device to
landscape. **Expected:** the race goes on in landscape. **Actual:** the race
freezes; "Pocket Quest isn't responding" after a few seconds.
**Attached:** the screenshot and the log line with RaceHud.cs:118.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note .ai-task title="Task with AI · A test plan for four setups"}
**Goal:** a test plan of 12 test cases for *Pocket Quest 1.3* on four
setups: the AVD P5_API_30, an AVD with API 26, a tablet AVD and the real P5.
By hand this takes long; the AI drafts, and you check and run.

1. **Ask the AI:** start with this prompt.

   ::: {.prompt}
   Write 12 test cases for a mobile racing game on Android, for these
   setups: an emulator with Android 11, an emulator with Android 8, a tablet
   emulator, and a real phone with 4 GB of RAM. For each test case give:
   the setup, numbered steps, and the expected result. Include tests of
   rotation, a phone call during a race, a slow network and a 20-minute
   race.
   :::

2. **Do it yourself:** check that each case has one clear setup, steps that
   someone else can follow, and an expected result you can see. Move the
   20-minute race and the tilt tests to the real phone.
3. **Check:** run two of the AI's cases in Emulator Lab or on your AVD. If a
   step cannot be done there, correct it.

*Your product:* the checked plan of 12 cases, and one sentence on what the
AI got wrong or what you changed.

::: {.check}
A good plan has 12 numbered cases, each with a setup, steps and an expected
result; the speed, heat and sensor tests are on the real P5; two cases were
run, with pass or fail. A typical change: "The AI put the 20-minute heat
test on the emulator, so I moved it to the real P5."
:::
:::

## Case study: Report Doctor

After the emulator session, six bug reports reach Byte Bay's developers:
one without the device, one without steps, one that says only "looks bad",
one without a build number, one with three bugs at once, and one without
any log or screenshot. The Game challenge of the interactive page uses
these reports. In the mini-game below you decide what must be fixed in each
one.

## Exercises

1. Name the three steps that create and start an AVD.
2. What is the difference between a cold boot and a quick boot?
3. adb prints `no devices/emulators found`. What do you do?
4. Which two kinds of evidence does a bug report need?
5. Why do you repeat a failed test case?
6. Name the parts of a good bug report.
7. Why one bug per report?

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. Create the device in the Device Manager, choose the profile and the
   system image, press Start.
2. A cold boot starts from zero and is slower; a quick boot uses a saved
   state.
3. Start the emulator, then check with `adb devices`.
4. A screenshot and the lines of the log (Logcat) around the error.
5. To be sure that the steps make the bug happen again.
6. Title, build, device and OS, steps, expected and actual result,
   attachments.
7. Each bug is fixed and checked on its own.
:::
